findings.source: return amounts; (uint256[] memory returned by each getter; solc 0.6 ABI encoding)
findings.issue: Every getter ends with the word-by-word copy of its result array into the return buffer printed as a loop (P7), after the real loop; the reader sees two loops per function where the source has one.
findings.rule: A loop copying 32 * n bytes word by word between disjoint memory ranges is one copy line (c00600's shape A); then 'return Array(len=n, data=...)'.

findings.source: SafeMath.sub(a, b) -> sub(a, b, "SafeMath: subtraction overflow") with require(b <= a, errorMessage) (solc 0.6, message passed as memory string)
findings.issue: The constant message is allocated in every iteration and copied by a loop into a half-decoded Error(string) revert, instead of revert with 'SafeMath: subtraction overflow'; 'assert s < mem[128]' is implied by the loop bound (P11).
findings.rule: A string written to fresh memory and only read by the Error(string) encoding of a revert is that literal (as c00561); drop the allocation and the copy loop.

notes: Source loops: one for loop per getter (15: getFees, getFullVaultTokenInfo, getFundingRates, getPairInfo ('while s < _14 / 2'), getPositions, getPrices, getStakingInfo, getTokenBalances, getTokenBalancesWithSupplies, getTokenSupply, getTotalBalance, getTotalStaked, getVaultTokenInfo, getVaultTokenInfoV2, getVestingInfo), all while. The 14 return-copy loops and getTokenSupply's message copy (311) are implicit (P7). P8: e.g. 'mem[x] = 0' then 'mem[x] = 0x18160ddd..' (273-274). All 26 ABI functions read.
summary: Every source loop is found and the getters match the source; each array getter adds a second, implicit copy loop for its return value, and SafeMath messages stay half-decoded reverts with copy loops.
